forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Lichfield leisure services audit finds limited assurance, second-lowest rating of four levels
news_drafts.lead: Lichfield's internal auditors have rated the council's leisure services as achieving only "limited assurance" — the second-lowest assurance level — identifying significant weaknesses in maintenance, health and safety oversight, business continuity planning, training compliance and debt recovery. The audit of the services, managed by trading company LWMTS, found multiple control failures with cash impact: when the new leisure centre opened, fibre-optic connectivity failures prevented income collection, causing an estimated revenue loss of £636, while leisure services currently holds £76,044 in outstanding customer balances, including £27,162 in aged debt. Ten member accounts are in arrears averaging £1,806 each, despite policy expecting members to fall into only one month's arrears. The council has no standalone business continuity plan for leisure services and relies instead on corporate arrangements with no documented contingencies for key systems or income collection.

news_drafts.headline: Lichfield reserves to fall below safety minimum as funding gap grows to £2.1m
news_drafts.lead: Lichfield Council's financial plan for the next four years shows an annual funding gap (the difference between day-to-day spending and available money) that starts at £50,000 in 2027/28 and grows to £2.1 million by 2029/30. The council is covering these shortfalls by drawing down its general reserves, the money set aside as a financial cushion. This is unsustainable: available reserves will fall from £3.3 million to £216,000 by 2030/31, well below the council's own minimum safe level of £2 million. The council has identified only £50,000 in annual proposed savings, meaning major decisions on council tax rises or service cuts must come by early 2027. The council faces additional structural uncertainty from the Government's Local Government Reorganisation programme, which may result in a merger with other councils.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report & Public Appendices
findings.headline: Section 106 developer contribution debt of £10,915 from 2019 left unrecovered; system automation gaps prevent effective debt identification
findings.detail: Testing of six Section 106 and Community Infrastructure Levy aged debts identified one application from 2019 with outstanding balance of £10,915 with limited evidence of recovery action. The Exacom system managing these contributions has automation limitations and relies on manual processes. System incorrectly classifies all outstanding applications as 'in debt' even where payment terms mean funds are not yet due, making aged debt reports unreliable for identifying truly overdue amounts.
findings.matters: Seven-year-old aged debt without documented recovery action indicates weak enforcement of developer contribution collection; system limitations mean council cannot rely on automated debt identification and escalation.
findings.figures: £10,915 outstanding on 2019 S106 debt; majority of tested debts misclassified by system
findings.quote: Testing of six debts included within the aged debt report identified that five related to applications where payments were either not yet due or were being paid in instalments in line with agreed terms. However, one debt dating back to 2019 had an outstanding balance of £10,915, with limited evidence of debt recovery action

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report & Public Appendices
findings.headline: Six audit recommendations are now overdue, having repeatedly missed implementation deadlines across multiple years
findings.detail: Six internal audit recommendations from prior years have now missed at least two implementation target dates and remain unresolved. These span 2017/18 Communications Strategy (awaiting Chief Executive approval), 2021/22 Microsoft 365 policy (awaiting approval), 2022/23 GDPR, 2024/25 Sundry Debtors and IT Revenues & Benefits audits, and 2025/26 Cyber Security remote working recommendations. Several overdue recommendations have no revised implementation dates provided.
findings.matters: Repeated failure to implement audit recommendations indicates weak management discipline in addressing identified control deficiencies; signals audit findings are not being prioritised despite documented governance gaps.
findings.figures: 6 recommendations overdue (missed 2+ implementation dates); 7 additional recommendations in progress
findings.quote: These recommendations have been marked as overdue as they have previously revised their implementation date. Therefore, they have now missed at least two implementation dates.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report & Public Appendices
findings.headline: Leisure services holds £76,044 in outstanding debts; 10 members in arrears averaging £1,806 each despite policy limiting to one month
findings.detail: Testing found leisure services holding £76,044 in total outstanding customer balances, of which £27,162 is aged. Audit identified 10 individual member accounts in arrears totalling £18,059 (average £1,806 per person), despite management expecting members to fall into only one month's arrears. Debt monitoring relies entirely on manual processes without automated alerts or system flags, causing delays in identification and collection.
findings.matters: Significant aged debt combined with failed controls indicates weak revenue collection governance and member arrears management failure; demonstrates manual processes are unreliable for debt escalation.
findings.figures: Total outstanding £76,044; aged debt £27,162; 10 accounts in arrears totalling £18,059
findings.quote: During discussions with the Leisure Director, we were informed individuals [...] only fall into one month's membership arrears. However, we found there were 10 individual accounts who had fallen into arrears, this totalled £18,059, an average of £1806 per person

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report & Public Appendices
findings.headline: New Lichfield Leisure Centre opening: fibre-optic connectivity issue caused £636 estimated revenue loss; no leisure-specific business continuity plan
findings.detail: When the new leisure centre opened, fibre-optic connectivity failures caused systems to become unavailable and prevented income collection, resulting in estimated revenue loss of approximately £636. Audit found neither the Council nor contractor LWMTS has a standalone business continuity plan for leisure services, instead relying on broader corporate arrangements with no documented contingency arrangements for key systems, sites, or income collection.
findings.matters: Service continuity failures during opening of new facility demonstrate operational resilience gaps; lack of documented contingency arrangements creates risk of recurrence and revenue loss.
findings.figures: Estimated revenue loss approximately £636; no documented leisure-specific business continuity plan
findings.quote: Management highlighted that when the new leisure centre opened, fibre-optic connectivity issues resulted in systems being unavailable and income being unable to be collected, leading to an estimated revenue loss of approximately £636

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report & Public Appendices
findings.headline: Leisure services control environment assessed as LIMITED assurance, the second-lowest of four assurance levels
findings.detail: The audit of Lichfield's leisure services, managed by trading company LWMTS, concluded with LIMITED assurance. Significant weaknesses were identified in maintenance and health & safety oversight, business continuity planning, training compliance, debt recovery processes, and non-financial performance reporting. Limited assurance indicates that system objectives are at substantial risk.
findings.matters: Limited assurance on a material council service signals material governance and control environment weaknesses; indicates substantial risk in service delivery and financial management oversight.
findings.figures: Leisure Centre audit concluded Limited Effectiveness Opinion
findings.quote: Overall, we conclude that the Council has a Limited level of assurance over the control environment supporting Leisure Services.
